and what to verify in the interview. If role_requirements are present, say in one

neither salesy nor alarmist.
Respond with JSON ONLY: {"summary": "..."}
user: {"notebook": "nb01_ana_ferreira.ipynb", "decision": "AVANCAR", "scores": {"C1": 5, "C2": 5, "C3": 5, "C4": 5}, "justifications": {"C1": "Methodology is sound: the notebook explicitly does a stratified train/test split before any preprocessing, and uses a Pipeline+ColumnTransformer so scaling/encoding are fit on X_tr only (cell 7). Other statements (e.g., low recall at 0.5 threshold) are consistent with RECALL_TEST=0.119 (cell 8).", "C4": "Conclusions are directly supported by outputs: top signals cited align with the largest-magnitude coefficients shown (cell 9) and the business recommendation targets the identified high-risk segment. response.summary: Overall, the notebook is high quality: it follows a correct modeling workflow, is readable, and appears reproducible end-to-end. The most important takeaway is that while discrimination is decent (AUC ~0.73), the model’s recall is very low at the default decision threshold, meaning it will miss many true positive cases unless the threshold/cost trade-off is tuned. In the interview, verify she can explain (in plain business terms) how she would choose and validate a decision threshold, and how she would design a more realistic validation strategy (e.g., time-based split if data has time effects). Against the stated role requirement, she meets “clean reproducible code” well through consistent pipelines, fixed random seeds, and a clear, executable structure.
